landing.headline: Know the ground before the convoy moves.
landing.body: Bhu-Rakshak watches rainfall, soil moisture, slope and earthquake shaking across Sikkim and the Darjeeling hills — and, as a preview, at hill towns across North-East India — and warns officials and residents when landslide risk rises.
landing.one_line: Live landslide risk for Sikkim, the Darjeeling hills and North-East India, for the officials who keep roads open and the people who travel them.
landing.predict_d: Rain, soil moisture, slope, rock type, earthquake shaking and past landslides combine into a live risk score for every monitored place.
landing.visualize_d: Officials see every corridor on one map, ranked by who and what is at stake.
landing.verify_d: Residents' reports and field checks confirm what the data shows.
landing.warn_d: Alerts reach residents in English or Hindi, with a loud alarm when the danger is high.

about.title: About & methodology
about.intro: Bhu-Rakshak is an early-warning and risk-management platform for landslides in Sikkim and the Darjeeling hills, with a preview across North-East India (Assam, Meghalaya, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram, Arunachal Pradesh), built by Team ByteMatrix for Smart India Hackathon 2026 (SIH26001).
about.p_data_d: Hourly rainfall, soil moisture at five depths, temperature, snow and freezing level for each place, refreshed every 30 minutes. Slope, rock type, vegetation, past landslides and exposure come from stored layers.
about.p_features_d: The raw data becomes landslide indicators: rain over 3, 24 and 72 hours, forecast rain, a soil saturation index, cloudburst and freeze–thaw flags.
about.p_model_d: A weighted model combines triggering and susceptibility factors into a score from 0 to 1, with a confidence value and the main drivers. Levels change with hysteresis so they don't flicker.
about.p_alerts_d: When a place rises to High or Critical, officers get a routed inbox message and residents get an alarm. Officers send bilingual alerts to the public.
about.p_feedback_d: Verified citizen and field reports mark a place as field-verified, which raises confidence and feeds future model training.
about.status_d: This prototype's main risk engine is a configurable baseline: transparent weights anchored on live Open-Meteo, IMD and earthquake data. Our machine-learning model runs alongside it as an experimental second opinion for officers. Slope, geology and exposure values are seed placeholders until official layers are connected. We don't claim accuracy beyond what our published backtests show.
about.c_openmeteo: Weather and soil-moisture data by Open-Meteo.com, licensed under CC BY 4.0.
about.c_bhuvan: Thematic overlays: Bhuvan, ISRO / NRSC (shown when the service is reachable).
about.c_boundary: India's boundary is drawn from an official Survey of India file supplied by the deployer.
about.c_google: In-person view: Google Street View, shown through Google Maps’ embed.
about.c_imd: Weather warnings and nowcasts: India Meteorological Department (IMD), Ministry of Earth Sciences.
about.c_esri: Satellite imagery: Esri World Imagery (Esri, Maxar, Earthstar Geographics and the GIS user community); road overlay © Esri.
about.c_osm: Street map: Esri World Street Map (Esri, HERE, Garmin, © OpenStreetMap contributors); terrain by OpenTopoMap (© OpenStreetMap contributors, SRTM).

ml.title: AI model (second opinion)
ml.inputs: Rain, last 3 days: {{rain3}} mm ({{ratio}}× normal) · heaviest hour in 48 h: {{hour}} mm · strongest recent shaking: {{mmi}} (MMI)
ml.no_data: No prediction for this place yet.
ml.accuracy: Tested on 2012–2016 landslides it never saw: caught {{caught}}% of landslides with warnings on {{fa}}% of ordinary days; {{right}}% of its warnings were right. It cannot yet tell which slope will fail.
ml.not_alerts: It does not trigger alerts — use it alongside the main risk score.
ml.track_none: Track record: no predictions logged yet.
ml.track_events: warned a day ahead for {{ahead}} of {{withAhead}} recorded landslides ({{day}} of {{n}} on the day or the day before);
ml.track_no_events: no confirmed landslides recorded near a monitored place yet;
ml.record_notes_hint: e.g. slide blocked NH-10 near the bridge
ml.record_help: Only confirmed landslides. The model is judged against — and retrained on — this record. Mistakes can be retracted, not deleted.
ml.retract_reason: Why is this record wrong? (kept in the audit log)
ml.dup_confirm: A landslide is already recorded within 2 km and 1 day. Record this one as a separate landslide?

preview.tip: Outside Sikkim/Darjeeling: filled automatically from public data; rock type and exposure not verified.
preview.note: Terrain, roads, rivers, vegetation and past landslides here were filled automatically from public data (SRTM, OpenStreetMap, MODIS, NASA landslide catalogue). Rock type, fault distance and people/facilities at risk are not verified yet — treat the risk level as indicative. Weather, earthquakes and the AI model run exactly as for Sikkim.
preview.note_plain: Some map data for this area hasn't been checked yet, so treat this level as a rough guide.

why.basis_plain: This is a guide based on rain, wet ground, slope and earthquakes, not a guarantee. Always follow official instructions.

corridor.title: Check a road corridor
corridor.intro: Pick where you start and where you are going. The route is split into about 2 km segments, each coloured by the landslide risk nearby.
corridor.tap_map: Tap the map to set the {{which}}
corridor.empty: Choose a start and a destination, then press “Check route”.
corridor.open_gmaps: Open this route in Google Maps
corridor.alt_error: Could not look for alternatives right now. Try again in a minute.
corridor.alt_none: No lower-risk route found nearby. If you must travel, go in daylight and check road status first.
corridor.alt_detour_note: Found by routing around the risky stretch. It may use smaller roads; check locally before you go.
corridor.method: Route from OpenStreetMap roads (OSRM). Each ~{{seg}} km segment takes the live risk level of the nearest monitored place within {{km}} km; farther segments are “not monitored”. Times are estimates; hill roads are often slower.

hindcast.eyebrow: Hindcast · replay of a real past landslide
hindcast.load_error: The replay data could not be loaded.
hindcast.callout: The system would have flagged {{place}} as {{level}} {{hours}} hours before the landslide.
hindcast.callout_none: The system would not have flagged {{place}} before this landslide.
hindcast.alarm_yes: That is High or above, so citizens nearby would have heard the alarm.
hindcast.alarm_no: It would not have reached High, so no alarm would have sounded. Moderate means “be careful, check before travelling”.
hindcast.at_event: Score at the time of the slide: {{score}} ({{level}}). High starts at {{high}}.
hindcast.map: Map of the landslide and the monitoring point
hindcast.chart_label: Risk score by hour with level bands, hourly rain below, the slide time and the chosen hour
hindcast.chart_hint: Tap or drag on the chart, or use the slider. Showing {{time}}.
hindcast.method_intro: We ran the same risk engine the live site uses, hour by hour, on archived data — using only what was known at each hour.
hindcast.limit_point: The live system scores one monitoring point for Aizawl, {{km}} km from where the slope failed; it does not watch every hillside.
hindcast.limit_rain: Rain comes from a weather model grid, not a rain gauge at the quarry. Local rain can be much heavier than the grid shows.
hindcast.limit_terrain: For North East preview places, rock type and fault distance are neutral defaults until field-verified.
hindcast.limit_one: One event is an example, not proof of how well the system works in general.
hindcast.data_file: Data file: /data/hindcast/event.json — generated by ml/build_hindcast.mjs from archived public data. To replay another event, change the event in the script and run it again.
hindcast.about_title: Would it have warned in time? A real replay
hindcast.about_body: We replayed a real past landslide in the North East through our live risk engine, hour by hour, using archived weather and only the information available at each hour — and we show the result as it is.
